- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast for next 5–10 days.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–4 days post-spike.  
- If 3+ consecutive days of model forecast > true outcome, apply mean reversion: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply a “lag correction”: subtract 0.5–1.5% from first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; adjust forecast to match sentiment trend direction by ±1–2% for next 3–7 days.
